column2: NOT PORTABLE, AND IT IS THEIR ONLY GEMM
column3: Every RAFT matrix product is legacy_gemm -> legacy_matmul -> cuBLASLt. There is no kernel in the RAPIDS tree to port: the arithmetic is inside a closed binary whose tile shape, k-split and (for CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F_FAST_TF32) mantissa width are chosen per vendor and per shape. PORTING_RULES.md 0b-i covers exactly this case -- call the MAX equivalent, because there is nothing to port -- and that is what core/gemm.mojo does under FAST. It is ALSO the reason this lane exists: a closed library cannot carry an identity claim, and a k-split IS a summation order (IDENTITY_PATHS rows 24, 28)

A standalone unfused port of it used to sit in core/gemm.mojo and was DELETED after measuring ~15 GFLOP/s against linalg.matmul's 248 at 1M x 128. column1: BATCHED GEMM (linalg.bmm.batched_matmul, and any upstream batched path)
column3: No production caller in this repository passes a batch dimension; the one appearance is mojo_only/vendor_correctness_check.mojo:1820, whose own header records it as NOT WIRED, and core/gram_splitk.mojo:28-33 rejects it for the Gram shape. What exists instead is HOST-SIDE TILE LOOPS (knn_brute_force.mojo query tiles, min_cluster_distance_compute.mojo centroid batches). Under contract sections 6 and 7 a batched GEMM CANNOT produce different bits from a loop of unbatched ones, because a cell's arithmetic depends on k and the profile alone and not on m, n or launch composition -- so batching is an EXECUTION PLAN feature, latency and not numerics. Deferring it costs nothing in the contract and adds nothing to it later

Contract section 10. alpha is one more rounding at a position that has to be specified; beta makes the output a function of C's prior contents, a second input the profile has not specified; bias is beta with a broadcast; epilogues are where the fused kernels live and the charter forbids disturbing them. core/column_stats.mojo::scale_in_place_kernel already exists because MAX's matmul has no alpha argument, so this repository's callers are already served by a separate pass

column1: FP16 / BF16 / TF32 inputs, integer and quantized dot products, float64
column3: Contract section 0.5. FP16/BF16 with FP32 accumulation is a modest follow-on profile; quantized inference is a separate substantial project (formats, dequantization, scaling, integer dot-product semantics, each its own ledger) and the charter says so explicitly. float64 does not exist on Metal
